title: Parser Internals
concept: The parser transforms tokens into an Abstract Syntax Tree (AST) — the structural representation of your program that all later passes use.
why: Understanding parsing reveals how your code's structure is understood. It explains why some expressions need parentheses and how operator precedence works.
tips: Pratt parsing handles operator precedence with minimal code — learn it once, use it everywhere
The AST is the intermediate representation that ALL later passes consume — get it right
Parser errors cascade — one missing brace causes many errors. Error recovery mitigates this
An AST can be 'pretty-printed' back to source code — useful for formatters and refactoring tools
common_mistakes: Parsing expressions without respecting precedence — '1 + 2 * 3' should be 7, not 9
Not handling left-recursion — can cause infinite loops in recursive descent parsers
Forgetting that the parser builds a TREE — order of evaluation is encoded structurally, not sequentially
